answer: Identity Renewal Cost Escalation. Each identity’s registration price rises along a shared cost ridge as more identities join within a rolling window, so the marginal fee for the next one tracks the tide of total signups rather than a fixed toll. An attacker who lets many puppets wander in during cheap off-peak periods finds that renewals compound at the peak rate they triggered, since lapsed identities re-enter at the elevated tier. Concretely, minting a thousand fresh identities costs the attacker escalating per-identity fees and forces continuous renewal spend to hold them.
